name: Maine

laws.summary: Authorizes the state CIO to set IT policies and standards, including ADA standards, which is the basis for the OIT accessibility policy.

laws.cite: 28 CFR Part 35, Subpart H (ADA Title II web & mobile rule, 2024; dates extended by IFR 2026-07663)
laws.summary: Federal floor: state and local government web content and mobile apps must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA; the April 2026 IFR moved compliance to 2027-04-26 (pop. 50,000+) and 2028-04-26 (smaller entities and special districts).

policy_docs.title: OIT Digital Accessibility and Usability Policy (v3.1, revised 2026-05-29)
State of Maine Accessibility (policy and laws)

applies_to: Digital information and services under the CIO's purview (executive branch agencies), public-facing and internal; archived and unmodified legacy content excepted.

deadlines.what: ADA Title II rule: state government and local governments with population 50,000+ must conform web content and mobile apps to WCAG 2.1 AA (extended from 2026-04-24 by DOJ IFR effective 2026-04-20)
ADA Title II rule: local governments under 50,000 and special district governments (extended from 2027-04-26)

requires: Conformance to Revised Section 508 and WCAG 2.1 A/AA
Agency mechanism for users to report accessibility issues
Equally Effective Alternative Access Plans (EEAAP) for content that is not accessible, approved by ADA/EEO coordinators
OIT Accessibility Team testing and application deployment certification
mobile: explicit — policy's software definition includes mobile client applications.
procurement: Vendors must submit an ACR on the newest VPAT (WCAG edition), filled out completely; OIT reviews ACRs and test results; procurement instruments with IT components must require compliance by default.
enforcement: CIO enforces the policy; waivers do not relieve federal/state obligations. Public complaints via agency reporting mechanism or Maine Human Rights Act / ADA.
notes: Policy first issued 2019-12-20; current v3.1 dated 2026-05-29. Statute URL taken from the policy's own footnote, not opened separately. No state-set compliance deadline found beyond ADA Title II.
